userMessages.text:
# Monorepo build and cache

Our monorepo build service supports local developers and CI. A change detector maps modified files to affected packages, and a build-graph service expands those packages to include required dependents and orders tasks by dependency. The scheduler assigns ready tasks to an elastic worker pool while allowing unrelated branches of the graph to run concurrently.

Before running a task, a worker calculates a content key from its sources, declared environment, toolchain version, command, and dependency outputs. It checks the remote cache and restores a matching result when one exists. A miss executes in an isolated workspace, uploads immutable outputs to the artifact store, and publishes the cache entry only after the task succeeds. Failed tasks are never cached, block their dependents, and return logs to the requesting developer or CI job. Cache entries carry provenance so results from untrusted forks cannot be reused by protected builds, and concurrent workers calculating the same key must converge without corrupting the entry.
